clearing_status.fact: SEC Acting Chair Uyeda stated at the 2026 U.S. Treasury Market Conference (sec.gov, Sept 22 2026): 'the SEC does not currently intend to extend these deadlines' of Dec 31 2026 (cash) and Jun 30 2027 (repo). The one-year extension granted Feb 25 2025 (90 FR 11134) remains the operative and only extension in force; no second extension has been announced as of Oct 19 2026.
clearing_status.rationale: Rubric score 1 requires 'an official extension granted' - the Feb 25 2025 one-year extension (90 FR 11134) satisfies this and remains the governing legal instrument. No second extension (score 2) has been issued, and the SEC's Sept 22 2026 statement explicitly rejects further extension, but the first extension is still in force and the original deadlines were already moved, keeping the rating at 1.

plan_financing.fact: 5-year JGB auction Oct 14 2026: bid-to-cover 3.56x (prev 3.42x, 12-month avg 3.36x), average yield 2.379% — firm demand (MOF/Reuters/Newsquawk, Oct 14 2026). 10-year JGB yield eased to ~2.91% on Oct 19 (TradingEconomics), down ~20bps from the ~3.12% peak in early October, as fund managers return to JGBs at elevated yields. Takaichi pledged Oct 5 to 'restrain' JGB issuance but without specifying a concrete supplementary budget funding mechanism (BigGo Finance/Reuters).
plan_financing.rationale: All post-Oct 9 auctions clear with bid-to-cover well above 3 and the 10-year yield has eased, ruling out Score 2 (disorderly). However, the supplementary budget funding path remains unspecified beyond vague 'restrain issuance' rhetoric, satisfying the Score 1 condition of 'funding path unspecified OR yield up >25bps but auctions clearing' — the funding-path arm of the OR keeps this at 1 despite improving market conditions.

direct_lending_default.fact: Fitch Ratings recorded a US Private Credit Default Rate (PCDR) of 6.3% for the trailing 12 months ended August 2026, up from 6.1% in July 2026 and a record high across ~1,300 borrowers, inclusive of distressed exchanges and liability-management exercises; 89 unique defaulters generated 109 default events in the TTM period. Source: Fitch Ratings report published September 15, 2026, as reported by The Lead PC (theleadpc.com/middle-market-private-credit-9-14-2026/) and Bloomberg (bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-14/us-private-credit-default-rate-hits-a-record-of-6-3-fitch-says).
direct_lending_default.rationale: The rubric anchors to Fitch's inclusive PCDR measure (counting distressed exchanges and LMEs); the August 2026 TTM print of 6.3% is the latest available Fitch figure, confirmed by the primary Fitch publication and corroborated by Bloomberg. No newer Fitch monthly print has been identified for September or October 2026, so the August reading is retained per rubric instructions.

dissent.view: Proskauer Private Credit Default Index: 2.51% for Q2 2026 (payment and financial-covenant defaults only, 716 loans, $195.6B original principal)
KBRA Middle Market Default Monitor: 3.3% by count and 2.4% by debt for TTM to 30 June 2026 (adds imminent defaults/interventions but not full LME scope)
Moody's private credit estimate: 1.6%-4.7% range for full-year 2025, depending on whether distressed exchanges are included

redemption_gates.fact: Fitch Ratings (reported Oct 13, 2026, via InvestmentNews/Blue Vault Oct 15) found nontraded BDC redemption requests averaged 9.8% across 13 of 15 perpetual-life funds in Q3 2026 — nearly twice the 5% quarterly cap — with named funds BCRED (~$79B, ~10% requests, prorated at 5% for third straight quarter per Sept 3 SEC letter), HLEND (~11.5%, prorated second consecutive quarter, ~$600M fulfilled per AltsWire Oct 2), CCLFX (~16%, capped at 5%), Blue Owl Credit Income Corp. (16.8%) and Blue Owl Technology Income Corp. (39%) all hitting 5% caps with proration; Stanger (Oct 2) counted $13.8B in Q3 requests across 19 funds with ~$8.2B unmet backlog.
redemption_gates.rationale: Five or more named large non-traded BDCs — including BCRED (~$79B) and CCLFX (~$31B) alone exceeding $100B combined AUM — had active 5% quarterly repurchase caps with proration in Q3 2026, satisfying the rubric's WIDESPREAD threshold of >=3 of the largest funds or combined gated AUM >$100B. No post-Oct 2 evidence indicates the gating has lifted; Fitch Oct 13 confirms elevated requests persist.

dissent.view: BDEBT (BlackRock) cleared its 5% tender cap without proration for first time in two quarters in Q3 2026 (requests fell to 4.58%), suggesting some funds are exiting gate territory; Golub GCRED also met requests in full at 4.8% in Q3. This partial easing does not change the WIDESPREAD reading given the number and AUM of funds still gated.

new_imf_programs.fact: Within the trailing 6-month window (Apr 19 – Oct 19 2026), the IMF Executive Board approved three new nonprecautionary lending arrangements: (1) Rwanda ECF, approved ~June 8 2026 (IMF PR 26/191); (2) Mauritania ECF+EFF, approved ~June 27 2026 (Panapress/IMF); (3) Bolivia EFF (36-month, ~US$1.9bn), Executive Board approval confirmed October 2 2026 (CGTN America; staff-level was July 29 2026 per IMF PR 26/268). No new sovereign missed coupons or distressed exchanges identified in the window (BoC-BoE Sovereign Default Database 2026 edition, published Oct 2026, records sovereign debt in default fell 14% in 2025 and flags no new 2026 defaults).
new_imf_programs.rationale: Three distinct sovereigns (Rwanda, Mauritania, Bolivia) received new Board-approved IMF lending arrangements inside the 6-month window; the rubric threshold for CLUSTER is 3 or more, yielding value 2. No sovereign defaults offset this count. [vintage guard: new read is 2026-10-02 data but the prior applied value was 2026-10-12 data; kept the newer vintage]
new_imf_programs.change_reason: new_event: Rwanda ECF (Jun 8 2026), Mauritania ECF+EFF (Jun 27 2026), and Bolivia EFF (Oct 2 2026) are three new Board-approved arrangements post-dating both the FY2026 Annual Report period and the prior Oct 12 reading window; the prior value of 0 was anchored solely to the FY2026 Annual Report (May 2025-Apr 2026) and missed these H2-2026 approvals.

dissent.view: IMF FY2026 Annual Report (May 2025-Apr 2026) records only 2 new nonprecautionary Board-approved arrangements for that fiscal year, which would suggest value 1 if one mistakenly uses the fiscal year as the trailing window rather than the rubric-specified calendar 6 months.

china_ppi.fact: China PPI rose +5.0% year-on-year in September 2026, per NBS press release published 14 October 2026 (stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202610/t20261015_1965499.html); corroborated by investing.com calendar (actual 5.0%, previous 3.8%), tradingeconomics.com, CNBC, and Caixin Global.
china_ppi.rationale: The rubric requires the signed NBS figure for the latest published month; the official NBS release of 14 October 2026 unambiguously reports +5.0% YoY for September 2026, up from +3.8% in August. This is a new post-2026-08 data point that supersedes the prior reading, triggering a value update.
china_ppi.change_reason: new_event: NBS released September 2026 PPI at +5.0% YoY on 14 October 2026, up from +3.8% in August 2026 — highest print since June 2022, driven by fuel and energy costs.

trade_actions.fact: As of Oct 17, 2026, at least 7 confirmed new major-economy trade measures against Chinese exports in the trailing 3 months: (1) US Section 301 forced-labor tariff of 12.5% on all Chinese goods, effective July 24, 2026 (91 FR 47318, federalregister.gov); (2) EU definitive AD on Chinese car/lorry tyres (4.3%-45.3%), July 7, 2026; (3) EU definitive AD on Chinese polyamide filament yarns (60%-67.6%), July 27, 2026; (4) EU AD investigation into PVC imports from China, September 2026; (5) EU launched 3 additional AD investigations into Chinese chemical products, September 2026 (confirmed by China MOFCOM, scio.gov.cn Oct 4, 2026); (6) EEU extended AD duties (12.23%-31%) on Chinese OCTG, EEC Resolution No. 127, Oct 6, 2026 (chemnet.com); (7) EU expiry review of Chinese wire rod AD duties (24% maintained), OJ Notice C/2026/5244, Oct 12, 2026; plus EU heads of state approved fast-track 'killer switch' tariff/quota powers on Chinese goods, Oct 17, 2026 (headtopics.com).
trade_actions.rationale: The count of new measures (>=7) far exceeds the rubric threshold of 4, and the US Section 301 forced-labor tariff alone constitutes a broad tariff round (12.5% across all Chinese goods), satisfying two independent ESCALATING triggers. No truce or rollback has been confirmed that offsets this count.

dissent.view: EU and China reached a preliminary deal in October 2026 in which China voluntarily agreed to cut EV exports to Europe by nearly half, suggesting some managed de-escalation in the EV sector specifically; however, this does not reverse the broader multi-sector escalation pattern.

license_flow.fact: MOFCOM Announcement No. 18 (April 4, 2025) — covering seven medium/heavy rare earths and derivative magnets including NdFeB (Dy/Tb-bearing) and SmCo — remains fully in force and unpaused as of 19 October 2026 (confirmed by technology.org status table dated 19 Oct 2026, chinaprospect.com as of 14 Oct 2026, and aihorizonnetwork.com as of 16 Oct 2026). General licences exist but are limited to named producers and pre-vetted customers; all others require per-shipment case-by-case review. Statutory window is 45 working days but actual approvals routinely run 60–120+ days per MERICS analysis cited by peacocktariffconsulting.com (14 Oct 2026). In the trailing 3 months: a 2026 licensing catalog added samarium/gadolinium/lutetium compounds; MOFCOM Announcement 26/2026 introduced an export-without-licence whistleblower reward scheme; and 10 U.S. firms (including MP Materials) were added to China's export control entity list on 22 June 2026. The October 2025 expansion (Announcements 55-58, 61, 62) remains suspended until 10 November 2026 with no formal legal extension published as of 16 October 2026.
license_flow.rationale: Per-shipment case-by-case licensing (not blanket/general coverage) and documented processing times of 60-120+ days — far exceeding the 30-day rubric threshold — satisfy the rubric's level 1 SLOWING criteria. New control-list additions within the trailing 3 months (compound catalog, U.S. entity list) add further level-1 triggers; no categorical denial to a country/sector or suspension of licensing issuance meets the level-2 threshold.

dissent.view: A MOFCOM official stated on 28 September 2026 that the truce suspension extends to January 2027, and U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent also publicly referenced this extension; if legally codified this would not alter the April 2025 regime's SLOWING status but would defer a potential level-2 escalation from the October package resuming.

truce_status.fact: The US-China rare-earth truce was extended to Jan 10, 2027 (Bessent, Sep 23 2026; MOFCOM official statement Sep 28 2026). As of Oct 19, 2026, that is 83 days away — inside the 90-day rubric window — with no further renewal announced. Critically, MOFCOM's legal text (Announcement No. 70, 2025) still reads 'until 10 November 2026'; as of Oct 16 no new MOFCOM announcement extending it has been published (MOFCOM 2026 list runs only to No. 48). US officials also confirm Chinese rare-earth deliveries remain materially below committed volumes, with yttrium exports down ~95% and magnet shipments to the US down 20% MoM in August 2026. (Sources: technology.org Oct 19 2026; mainrichinternational.com updated Oct 11 2026; rareearthexchanges.com Oct 2026; startupfortune.com Oct 8 2026)
truce_status.rationale: At 83 days to the nominal Jan 10 2027 expiry with no renewal announced, the rubric's '90 days or fewer to expiry with no renewal announced' trigger is now definitively crossed, placing this squarely at score 1. The unresolved MOFCOM legal-text gap (Announcement 70 unchanged as of Oct 16) and persistent compliance shortfalls further confirm the 'fraying' characterisation rather than 0 or 2.

dissent.view: China's MOFCOM Announcement No. 70 still legally reads 'until 10 November 2026' as of Oct 16, with no published extension notice — implying China's legal pause could lapse Nov 10, which would push toward score 2 if unresolved

re_blacklist.fact: MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026 (22 June 2026) placed MP Materials Corp. and USA Rare Earth Inc. on China's Export Control List, banning all parties from supplying Chinese-origin dual-use items to those two named firms; the listing remained confirmed active as of 16 August 2026 (materialsdispatch.com) with no removal or sector-wide extension detected. Source: MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026; corroborated by Benchmark Minerals (2026-06-22), S&P Global (2026-06-22), Morgan Lewis (2026-07-01), materialsdispatch.com (2026-08-16).
re_blacklist.rationale: Two named US rare-earth producers (MP Materials Corp. and USA Rare Earth Inc.) are on the MOFCOM Export Control List by firm name, satisfying rubric value 1. The measure is explicitly entity-specific, not a categorical sector-wide ban, as confirmed by Benchmark Minerals: 'The measure is entity-specific rather than a blanket restriction on rare earth exports to the US.'

hree_premium.fact: Fastmarkets assessed dysprosium oxide 99.5% CIP global at $2,500-3,500/kg (week ended Oct 1, 2026), against China domestic of ~$210/kg (SMM oxide), implying a midpoint multiple of ~14-16x; REEx (Oct 13, 2026) separately reported $3,250-3,500/kg ex-China vs $209-215/kg domestic (~15-16x). Source: Fastmarkets (fastmarkets.com, Oct 1 2026); Rare Earth Exchanges (rareearthexchanges.com, Oct 13 2026).
hree_premium.rationale: The Fastmarkets CIP global benchmark mid (~$3,000/kg) divided by the SMM China domestic oxide price (~$210/kg) yields ~14.3x; the upper-bound transaction evidence (REEx Oct 13) points to ~15-16x, averaging to ~15x. This is a modest downward revision from the 16.3x Q3-end BMI CIF Europe figure, reflecting the Fastmarkets CIP global mid settling slightly below the Q3 peak, not a structural regime change.
hree_premium.change_reason: new_event: Fastmarkets CIP global dysprosium oxide benchmark (week ended Oct 1 2026) assessed at $2,500-3,500/kg, implying a midpoint multiple of ~14.3x; REEx Oct 13 2026 corroborates ~15-16x range, placing the best single estimate at ~15x versus the prior 16.3x CIF Europe BMI peak.

dissent.view: REEx (Oct 17, 2026) reports up to $5,500/kg ex-China vs ~$200/kg China, implying up to ~27x — but REEx itself flags this as a thin-market scarcity ceiling on legally-sourced verified material, not a liquid benchmark
REEx (Oct 2, 2026) notes a wide 3-17x range for dysprosium ex-China, reflecting the absence of a single liquid spot market and varying transaction provenance

genius_impl.fact: As of October 19, 2026, the GENIUS Act Section 13 statutory rulemaking deadline of July 18, 2026 has been missed by all primary federal regulators (OCC, Federal Reserve, FDIC, NCUA, Treasury/FinCEN/OFAC) — zero final rules published. The OCC targets a final rule by November 2026; the Federal Reserve issued its NPRM only on September 24, 2026 with comments open until November 30, 2026; Treasury's Section 3 NPRM comment period closed today (October 19, 2026); one Treasury interim final rule (Federal Register 2026-19966, Sept 30) covers state certification procedures only. The statutory effective date defaults to the January 18, 2027 backstop. (Sources: coinpedia.org Oct 19 2026; frame.xyz; fintechlaw.ai; yahoo finance/willkie Oct 5 2026)
genius_impl.rationale: The rubric assigns 2 = PROBLEMS when the deadline is missed without final rules — confirmed: all seven agencies missed July 18, 2026 with no final implementing rules across OCC, Fed, FDIC, NCUA, or Treasury as of today. No court stay or compliance-failure event is needed to reach level 2; the deadline miss alone with zero finalized rules satisfies the criterion.

ai_revenue_gap.fact: Microsoft FY26Q3 (Apr 29 2026, microsoft.com/investor): capex $30.9B up ~85% YoY; AI business ARR $37B up 123% YoY; Azure grew 40% YoY (5th consecutive quarter of acceleration). Combined hyperscaler 2026 capex guided ~$725B (+77% YoY vs ~$410B in 2025). Q3 calendar 2026 earnings not yet reported (MSFT/GOOGL Oct 28, AMZN Oct 29, 2026).
ai_revenue_gap.rationale: Capex growth (~77-85% YoY) exceeds AI-attributable revenue growth in absolute dollar terms, but AI revenue is strongly accelerating YoY (+123%) with no deceleration QoQ and no hyperscaler has cut its AI-revenue outlook — this is the definition of rubric value 1 (WIDE). No new post-April-2026 earnings data exists to change this reading; the next earnings cycle reports Oct 28-29 2026.

regional_bank_stress.rationale: Exactly 1 CRE-linked failure in the trailing 6-month window, with assets of $736M (well below $10B threshold); no single failure >$10B, no interagency emergency facility, and no new post-Oct-12 event. This maps mechanically to ISOLATED (1-2 such failures each <$10B). [cross-check (asi1): two reads disagreed (1 vs 0); held for review]

govt_stability.fact: CNBC (24 Sep 2026) reports Lecornu still PM, describing 'the probable last months of his premiership' and a new 2027 budget battle; Wikipedia confirms Second Lecornu government (formed 10 Oct 2025) is 'incumbent' minority coalition with no dissolution recorded. Most recent no-confidence vote found (~22 Apr 2026) secured 282 votes, 7 short of the 289 threshold, government survived.
govt_stability.rationale: The Second Lecornu government is a minority cabinet that has repeatedly invoked Article 49.3 and survived multiple no-confidence votes without falling; this squarely maps to rubric band 1 (FRAGILE: minority/hung parliament relying on Art. 49.3 or surviving no-confidence votes, but governing). No evidence of collapse, PM resignation, or dissolution post-12 Oct 2026.

rating_action.fact: Per AFT (aft.gouv.fr, accessed Oct 2026): Moody's rates France Aa3/Negative (last action 10 Apr 2026, next review 23 Oct 2026 - not yet occurred); S&P rates France A+/Stable (29 May 2026); Fitch rates France A+/Stable (28 Aug 2026). The S&P and Fitch downgrades from autumn 2025 (Fitch 12 Sep 2025; S&P 18 Oct 2025) have now aged beyond the 12-month trailing window as of 2026-10-19, so rubric band 2 no longer applies.
rating_action.change_reason: correction: The prior value of 2 relied on the autumn 2025 S&P/Fitch downgrades being within the trailing 12 months; as of 2026-10-19 both are at or beyond that boundary (Fitch >13 months ago, S&P ~366 days ago), so the load-bearing fact reverts to Moody's still-active Negative outlook, placing the reading at 1.

dissent.view: IBISWorld cites Fitch data showing June 2026 subprime 60+ day delinquency at 5.67% (vs. Fitch-reported 5.80% for June); minor methodological or rounding difference, not a material conflict with the July 6.13% reading.

ankso.blog cites Fitch data showing the rate eased to 5.49% by May 2026 (lowest since May 2024), slightly diverging from other sources that put the May trough closer to 5.49-5.80%; directionally consistent but numerically distinct from the July rebound figure.

bnpl_delinq.rationale: 30+ DPD is up ~20 bps YoY — clearly rising but far below the 100 bps threshold for level 2; charge-offs remain below 5% (CFPB pay-in-four rate 1.83%, Affirm lifetime vintage NCO ~3.5% GMV), so rubric maps to 1 (rising, charge-offs contained). dollar_reserve_share.fact: IMF COFER data brief published 30 September 2026 (data.imf.org / centralbanking.com): the dollar's share of foreign exchange reserves was 56.7% at end-June 2026, down from 57.13% in Q1 2026. Source: https://data.imf.org/en/news/imf%20data%20brief%20september%2030 and https://www.centralbanking.com/central-banks/economics/data/7977210/dollars-share-of-foreign-reserves-fell-slightly-in-q2-imf
dollar_reserve_share.rationale: The rubric requires reporting the latest USD share of allocated global FX reserves as a percent; the most recent official IMF COFER release (30 Sep 2026) gives 56.7% for Q2 2026, which maps directly to the rubric value. No Q3 2026 COFER data exists yet (next release expected ~Dec 2026), so the Q2 2026 figure remains the authoritative current reading.

weaponization_event.fact: The New Delhi Declaration (Sep 12-13, 2026) formally endorsed BRICS Pay as a local-currency settlement interoperability layer, but per Eastern Herald and Rio Times Online analysis: BRICS Pay 'does not create a reserve asset, a clearing mechanism backed by member-state central banks, or any instrument that would allow a country to hold BRICS Pay balances the way it holds dollar reserves.' On 12 Oct 2026 the EU adopted ~1,569 new Russia military-industrial listings (largest-ever round), extending asset freezes; however, as of Oct 19, 2026 Rio Times Online confirms the Russian reserve principal 'remains legally contested and politically blocked' with no new outright sovereign seizure executed. No new sovereign reserve freeze of a previously unaffected country has been identified.
weaponization_event.rationale: BRICS Pay endorsement and new EU listings extensions are settlement-system rhetoric/incremental sanction maintenance — not a new sovereign reserve seizure or a major economy operationally moving off USD settlement — placing this squarely in band 1 (TALK). No evidence of a band-2 triggering event (new reserve freeze/seizure or major economy operationally departing USD settlement rails) was found in the post-2026-10-10 window.

dissent.view: Some outlets (informedclearly.com) assert 'BRICS Pay Goes Live' and frame it as a dollar-free settlement launch, implying a more operational shift; however these sources are not primary/authoritative and conflict with more rigorous analysis from Modern Diplomacy and Eastern Herald showing BRICS Pay remains a payment-messaging pilot, not a reserve-settlement departure.

insurer_exits.fact: Weiss Ratings (Sep 8, 2026) analysis of NAIC 2025 MCAS filings named Utah the new nonrenewal epicenter at 4.45% of policies, ahead of CA (2.93%) and FL; Foster (2026) documented elevated nonrenewal rates in 13 states (many Midwest + CA/FL/LA); NAIC August 2026 report confirmed company-initiated nonrenewal rates rose 96%-216% across all four U.S. regions (2018-2024). No top-10 homeowners insurer fully exited a major state in 2026: State Farm CA rate settlement became final Jul 23, 2026 with pledge of no new block non-renewals; Allstate filed to RETURN to CA new business Sep 1, 2026; Farmers eliminated its cap Nov 2025. Sources: NAIC/CNBC Aug 2026; Weiss Ratings/Newsweek Sep 8, 2026; AdvoraHQ Oct 2026.
insurer_exits.rationale: Elevated nonrenewal waves are documented across approximately 13 states (5-15 range), satisfying the rubric's level-1 threshold of 'elevated across 5-15 states but some markets stabilizing.' The level-2 trigger (>15 states OR a top-10 insurer fully exiting a major state) is not met, as State Farm settled and committed to staying in CA, and Allstate filed to re-enter CA.

dissent.view: Some secondary sources cite 'at least 6 states' with sudden non-renewal notices in 2026 (roofingacademy.com citing The Queen Zone), which would be a lower count than the 13 documented by Foster (2026) using NAIC MCAS data; this lower figure reflects only reported consumer-facing incidents, not the full regulatory dataset.

cat_losses.fact: H1 2026 global insured nat-cat losses: USD 42bn (Swiss Re Institute, Aug 11 2026), 16% below the 10-yr H1 avg of ~USD 50bn; Munich Re confirms USD 44bn (Jul 30 2026); Aon estimates USD 47bn. Post-cutoff: Hurricane Isaias (Cat 2, Oct 9 landfall near Destin FL) insured losses estimated at USD 1-3bn by Verisk/KCC/Cotality, USD 2.5-4.5bn by Moody's RMS (best estimate USD 3.5bn); AM Best calls it an 'earnings event'; Gallagher Re says it will not influence Jan 1 renewals (Oct 15 2026). No single 2026 event exceeds USD 10bn.
cat_losses.rationale: YTD insured losses remain below the 10-year average even after adding Isaias (~USD 3bn), and no single 2026 event has breached the USD 10bn threshold; both rubric conditions for ELEVATED (score 1) are unmet. Isaias is an idiosyncratic, sub-threshold earnings event for the industry, not a systemic shock.

dissent.view: Moody's RMS best estimate for Isaias is USD 3.5bn (range USD 2.5-4.5bn), slightly above KCC's USD 3bn point estimate, but both are well below the USD 10bn rubric threshold

ss_reform_news.fact: As of September 28, 2026, H.R. 9187 (Bipartisan Social Security Commission Act) remains in committee with no floor action, and S.4979 (PROMISE Act, introduced July 14, 2026) was introduced in Senate but has not passed either chamber. The 2026 SSA Trustees Report (June 9, 2026) projects OASI trust fund depletion in Q4 2032 (one quarter earlier than 2025), combined OASDI depletion Q3 2034, and a 75-year actuarial deficit of 4.42% of payroll. No automatic benefit cut has been triggered; benefits have not been reduced. Source: financebuzz.com citing congress.gov (Sept 28, 2026); ssa.gov/oact (June 9, 2026); crfb.org (June 9, 2026).
ss_reform_news.rationale: The 2026 Trustees Report worsened the depletion date and multiple reform bills are actively debated, squarely meeting rubric band 1 (DEBATE). No enacted cuts or triggered automatic reductions have occurred, so band 2 (CUTS) is not met.

pension_leverage_event.fact: BoE FPC Record – April 2026 (bankofengland.co.uk/financial-policy-committee-record/2026/april-2026): 'The FPC noted that the liability driven investment (LDI) sector had remained resilient in the current market environment,' supported by post-2022 liquidity buffer requirements (min 250 bps FPC/TPR). Corroborated by the BoE July 2026 Financial Stability Report (no LDI stress flagged) and IFS analysis published 12 October 2026 explicitly stating '2026 is not a rerun of 2022' on LDI.
pension_leverage_event.rationale: All authoritative post-September-2026 sources confirm LDI buffers are adequate and no margin-call episode or forced selling has occurred; this maps squarely to rubric level 0 (NONE). No new event after 2026-09-25 changes the prior reading.

funded_ratio.fact: Milliman 100 Public Pension Funding Index (PPFI) funded ratio: 88.2% as of July 31, 2026, covering the 100 largest U.S. public defined benefit plans. Source: Milliman PPFI August 2026 update (published August 27, 2026), https://sg.finance.yahoo.com/news/milliman-analysis-public-pension-funded-180000985.html (Business Wire / Milliman). No subsequent PPFI monthly update (August or September 2026 data) has been published as of the search date.
funded_ratio.rationale: The August 27, 2026 Milliman PPFI release is the most recent authoritative public-pension funded-ratio data point; 88.2% maps directly to the rubric's requested representative large US public-pension funded ratio. The October 7, 2026 Milliman release covers corporate pensions (PFI, 114.5%), a distinct index not applicable to this rubric.

interconnection_months.fact: LBNL Queued Up: 2026 Edition (data workbook updated May 2026, PDF published June 2026, emp.lbl.gov/queues): 'The median project built in 2025 took 61 months from the interconnection request to commercial operations' — down from 63 months for the 2024 in-service cohort.
interconnection_months.rationale: The rubric calls for the latest published median IR-to-COD in months from LBNL; the 2026 Edition is the most recent release and reports 61 months for the 2025 in-service cohort. No newer LBNL edition exists as of 2026-10-19, so the value remains 61.

dc_moratoria.fact: electricchoice.com (updated ~Oct 16, 2026) reports '575 [moratoriums] currently in force across 46 states'; New York EO 62 (Jul 14, 2026) remains the first confirmed statewide moratorium; Texas Gov. Abbott directed TCEQ to halt data-center permits (Newsweek, ~Oct 2026); Oregon Gov. Kotek directed a state-level pollution-permit pause through July (Oct 14, 2026); plus hundreds of enacted local/county moratoria across FL, MD, TN, WA, CA, OR and others confirmed by dcmap.us tracker (Oct 7, 2026).
dc_moratoria.rationale: Rubric level 2 requires 'a statewide moratorium enacted OR >10 jurisdictions with enacted pauses.' New York EO 62 alone satisfies the statewide threshold, and multiple additional state-level executive orders (TX, OR, and ~11 others per electricchoice.com) plus 575 local actions in force across 46 states confirm deep exceedance of the >10-jurisdiction sub-criterion; value remains 2.

dissent.view: apog.ai (Oct 2, 2026) states '0 [state moratorium bills] were signed into law' as of that date — a narrow legislative-only reading that excludes executive orders including NY EO 62, TX, and OR governor directives.
ailawsbystate.com (Oct 8, 2026) similarly notes no state legislature enacted a statewide moratorium, treating EO 62 as executive-only, not a legislative enactment.

ai_power_pressure.fact: FERC on Oct. 9, 2026 rejected PJM's IRAS curtailment framework and BYONC rules, leaving a confirmed 6,831 MW PJM capacity shortfall (2028/29 delivery year) unresolved; separately, Texas PUCT Docket 59220 on July 24, 2026 imposed a 525.5 MW emergency curtailment obligation on two co-located data centers, and DOE 202(c) orders authorizing PJM data-center curtailment were in force July 1-3, 2026 during a record 168,158 MW peak. Sources: Utility Dive Oct. 12 2026; mgrid.org Oct. 10 2026; safeguard.sh (citing PUCT Docket 59220, July 24 2026); electricchoice.com (DOE orders July 1-3 2026).
ai_power_pressure.rationale: Confirmed physical curtailment obligations have been imposed (Texas July 24, PJM July 1-3) within or near the 90-day window; the structural 6,831 MW PJM shortfall is confirmed and the FERC Oct. 9 rejection of the IRAS framework leaves no systematic forward curtailment tool in place, sustaining acute grid stress. This maps unambiguously to rubric level 2 (confirmed curtailment of data-center load and a declared grid emergency).

dissent.view: FERC rejected PJM's proposed forward curtailment plan on Oct. 9, which could be read as easing acute curtailment *risk* for new loads — but this does not undo existing confirmed curtailment events or the capacity shortfall; it merely removes a prospective management tool.

mine_disruptions.fact: As of mid-October 2026, at least four top-20 copper mines have confirmed active production cuts: (1) Grasberg Block Cave (world #2): Q1 2026 output only 95 Mlb vs ~425 Mlb normal quarterly rate per Freeport 8-K; Gresik smelter also shut Aug 2026 for boiler repairs; full restart delayed to early 2028 (Northern Miner, May 8 2026; Freeport 8-K Q1 2026; GuruFocus Aug 11 2026). (2) Kamoa-Kakula (top-5): 2026 guidance cut from 380,000-420,000 t to 290,000-310,000 t (Ivanhoe Q2 results, July 29 2026; SMM). (3) Escondida (world #1): shut after fatal accident Sep 2026, removing ~3,455 t/day; no restart timeline set (cruxinvestor, Sep 2026). (4) Centinela (Antofagasta, top-20): strike by 700+ workers since Oct 7 2026, ongoing as of Oct 16 2026 (mining.com Oct 8; Bloomberg Oct 14 2026). ING forecasts 600 kt refined copper deficit for 2026; JPMorgan 330 kt; Benchmark ~400 kt.
mine_disruptions.rationale: Four confirmed top-20 mines have active, verified production cuts simultaneously - Grasberg (still in phased ramp-up, secondary smelter outage Aug 2026), Kamoa-Kakula (guidance cut ~90,000-130,000 t below original), Escondida (fatal-accident shutdown Sep 2026), and Centinela (active strike Oct 2026) - easily meeting the CLUSTER threshold of >=3 major mines disrupted; multiple institutions forecast a market deficit of 330-600 kt in 2026, satisfying the alternative CLUSTER trigger as well.
mine_disruptions.change_reason: new_event: Escondida (world #1) shut after fatal accident Sep 2026 with no restart timeline; Centinela strike began Oct 7 2026 (700+ workers, ongoing as of Oct 16); Antofagasta cut Los Pelambres guidance after Jul 2026 weather/power outages; these post-Oct-12 developments add a third and fourth concurrent major-mine disruption beyond the two already counted, reinforcing value=2 with additional corroborating events

dissent.view: Panmure Liberum (as cited by mining.com.au) argues total 2025-26 copper mine disruptions amount to only 350,000-400,000 t/yr, equivalent to only 30-50% of published disruption allowances, implying the market impact is less severe than headline events suggest

copper_deficit_timing.fact: ICSG October 2026 forecast (issued 15 Oct 2026): global refined copper market surplus of ~104,000 metric tons in 2026, widening to ~368,000 mt in 2027; source: Mining Weekly / Northern Miner / IndexBox citing ICSG, dated 15-16 October 2026.
copper_deficit_timing.rationale: A forecast surplus of +104,000 kt for 2026 is unambiguously above zero and well outside the +/-100kt balanced band, satisfying rubric level 0 (SURPLUS). The April 2026 reading of +96kt has been modestly revised upward to +104kt, confirming the surplus characterisation is intact.
copper_deficit_timing.change_reason: new_event: ICSG October 2026 meeting (15 Oct 2026) updated the 2026 refined copper balance to a surplus of ~104,000 mt, slightly larger than the April 2026 figure of ~96,000 mt but same rubric outcome (0 = SURPLUS).

drought_chip_farm.fact: As of October 16, 2026, Taiwan's 22 tracked reservoirs (WRA data via reservoirs.earth) hold 60.8% of combined capacity, described as 'within their normal operating range' with 'none of the tracked reservoirs currently at critically low levels'; key Hsinchu chip-hub feeders (Baoshan 1, Baoshan 2, Shimen) were at or near 100% by mid-August 2026. The March 27, 2026 WRA rationing order was set to expire in July 2026 and no source confirms it remains in force. Source: reservoirs.earth citing WRA, 2026-10-16; WRA live data 2026-08-14.
drought_chip_farm.rationale: The March 2026 rationing order is now more than 90 days old and reservoir data confirms substantial recovery post-typhoon season, meeting the rubric's band-1 criterion ('earlier rationing order that has since been lifted, with no production impact now'). Band-2 requires a rationing order IN FORCE today or imposed within the last 90 days, which is not confirmed by any current source. [reversal guard: 2 -> 1 would undo the change made on 2026-10-12; held at 2 until a second consecutive read confirms it]
drought_chip_farm.change_reason: new_event: Taiwan reservoir levels recovered to ~61% nationally (WRA/reservoirs.earth, 2026-10-16) following typhoon-season rainfall, with Hsinchu fab-hub feeders at ~100%; the March 2026 rationing order had a stated July 2026 expiry and no source confirms it remains in force, removing the confirmed-in-force rationing that justified value=2.

reservoir_stress.fact: Lake Mead elevation 1,037.31 ft, storage ~6,801,830 acre-feet, 26.0% of USBR active capacity (26,120,000 AF basis) as of Oct 16-17, 2026 — a new all-time record low since first filling; minimum power pool is 950 ft, reservoir ~87 ft above that threshold. Sources: USBR Upper Colorado hydrodata via reservoirbench.com, hydrostatus.com, lakemead.hydromap.com, Wikipedia (citing USBR).
reservoir_stress.rationale: At 26.0% of active capacity, Lake Mead is well below the 30% CRITICAL threshold in the rubric; storage has continued to decline since the Oct 11 reading (1,037.71 ft / 26.1%) to a new record low, keeping it firmly in the CRITICAL band.

dissent.view: lakelevelnow.com reports 23% full at 1,037.4 ft on Oct 17, 2026 — slightly lower percentage than other sources, likely due to a different capacity basis (possibly total vs. active capacity)

water_dispute.fact: India's IWT abeyance (declared April 2025) remains in force as of 15 October 2026. Pakistan's Ambassador raised it at the European Parliament on 15 Oct 2026; Pakistan's Deputy PM Dar briefed the UN Secretary-General on 6 Oct 2026. The PCA ruled 31 Aug 2026 the treaty is still binding; India rejected the ruling and reconfirmed abeyance. No armed clash, deliberate flow cut-off, or explicit head-of-state war threat has been reported. Sources: nation.com.pk (15 Oct 2026), pakera.pk (6 Oct 2026), Al Jazeera (31 Aug 2026).
water_dispute.rationale: The IWT remains formally in abeyance/contested — a standing condition that fits rubric band 1 (TENSE: treaty formally contested or in abeyance). No event since 12 October 2026 or within the prior 90 days meets the level-2 threshold of armed clash, deliberate cut-off, or explicit head-of-state war threat.

fao_food_trend.fact: FAO Food Price Index averaged 136.0 points in September 2026, up 2.0 points (+1.5%) MoM from revised August and +5.8% YoY; third consecutive monthly increase and highest since November 2022. Source: FAO (fao.org/worldfoodsituation/foodpricesindex), released 2 October 2026.
fao_food_trend.rationale: MoM change of +1.5% is below the 5% SPIKING threshold and the index is rising and at a multi-year high, placing it squarely in rubric band 1 (ELEVATED). The 3-month cumulative rise does not reach 10% given July edged down before August-September increases.

china_export_curbs.fact: Per Argus Media cited by UkrAgroConsult (Oct 16 2026) and global-agriculture.com (Oct 19 2026): China's phosphate fertilizer exports have fallen from 5.3 mln tonnes in 2025 to 'almost nothing' in 2026; ChemAnalyst (c. Oct 15 2026) notes traders in September 2026 'expected exports might not resume this year.' Urea exports continue under a controlled quota (3.3 Mt cap with FOB floors of $430-440/t per GIDEX/DiscoveryAlert Sep 2026), with actual shipments possibly reaching 6-7 Mt per Argus forecast. The original NDRC-linked phosphate suspension (Dec 2025, extended Mar 2026 to cover NK blends and additional phosphate varieties) formally ran to Aug 31 2026 but the de facto suspension continues post-deadline with near-zero shipments confirmed.
china_export_curbs.rationale: Both phosphate suspension and urea quota remain operationally in force as of mid-October 2026 with no post-Aug 31 formal reinstatement or new tightening confirmed - the restrictions continue unchanged in effect, mapping squarely to rubric value 1 (existing quotas/suspensions continue). No NEW product added or quota lowered after 2026-08-31 is documented, ruling out value 2.

dissent.view: Urea exports forecast at 6-7 Mt for full-year 2026 (Argus Media via UkrAgroConsult Oct 2026), materially above the 3.3 Mt formal quota, suggesting quota was revised upward or selectively waived - consistent with Aug 2026 Food Security Portal noting 'expanded Chinese export quotas' for nitrogen
GlobalTradeAlert records the March 2026 export ban revocation date as Aug 31 2026, implying formal expiry - but post-expiry physical data show near-zero phosphate exports continuing

hormuz_fertilizer.fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day (2.4% of baseline); straits.live Oct 19 2026 daily brief, sourcing portwatch.imf.org feed.
hormuz_fertilizer.rationale: 2 transits/day is 2.4% of the 85/day baseline, far below the 25% threshold required to exit the CUT band; Gulf sulfur exports fell 33% in H1 2026 (IFPRI) and Qatar suspended urea/ammonia/sulfur production (World Bank/chemicalsblog), fully corroborating the transit-based rating. Transit count worsened post-Oct 12 (4→2) and attacks escalated (two ships sunk Oct 14-15, sea-mine strike Oct 19), so no basis to change the value.

dissent.view: US military claims 97% of ships transit safely despite Iranian attacks — a figure straits.live notes it cannot independently assess and which contradicts AIS-based PortWatch counts

taiwan_tension.fact: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense official bulletin (mnd.gov.tw, issued 2026-10-19) recorded 5 PLA aircraft sorties, 6 PLAN ships and 9 official ships around Taiwan in the 24 hours to 0600 19 Oct, with 3 sorties crossing the median line into Taiwan's ADIZ. The Liaoning carrier strike group conducted 'routine drills' in the western Pacific from ~14 Oct before transiting toward the South China Sea. The MSA-notified coastal live-fire zones (12-17 Oct, five sea areas) concluded on schedule with no zones encircling Taiwan. Focus Taiwan/CNA (15 Oct) confirms the PLA has not staged a large-scale encirclement exercise in 2026, and no new MSA no-sail notices encircling Taiwan have been issued.
taiwan_tension.rationale: Persistent median-line crossings and a carrier strike group deployment are assertive gray-zone operations consistent with rubric level 1 (large-scale assertive patrols/drills), but there is no encirclement exercise, no blockade, and no kinetic clash, ruling out level 2. Activity is materially above routine level 0.

export_controls.fact: On 16 October 2026, MOFCOM and MOST issued Announcement [2026] No. 48 proposing export controls on 40 technologies (23 in AI), with a temporary registration requirement effective immediately; prior Chinese countermeasures also active: July 2026 addition of Rheinmetall and Dutch entities to China's Export Control List, June 22 2026 MOFCOM dual-use supply bans on 10 US companies. On the US/allied side, MATCH Act (DUV ban bill) remains pending in Congress (introduced April 2, 2026); core BIS controls (Entity List, FDP Rule, fab-equipment restrictions) remain in force per BIS.gov and ASML 2025 Annual Report (SEC, 2026). Sources: Baker McKenzie (Oct 16 2026), CFR (Sept 2026), ASML 6-K (2026), techwireasia.com (Oct 15 2026).
export_controls.rationale: Both the US/allied side (ongoing BIS/NL/EU controls, MATCH Act advancing) and China (MOFCOM Announcement No. 48 AI tech export controls effective Oct 16, July 2026 ECL additions of Dutch entities, June 2026 dual-use bans) have active measures within the trailing 90 days, satisfying rubric level 2 (retaliation: target country enacts countermeasures). No change from prior reading; same structural conditions confirmed with new Oct 16 Chinese action adding marginal support.

dissent.view: ASML 2025 Annual Report notes the US Affiliates Rule is suspended until Nov 10 2026 and China rare-earth Oct 9 measures also suspended, suggesting partial de-escalation truce — one could argue the bilateral suspension agreement partially offsets escalation, keeping the rubric closer to 1; however active measures on both sides remain unreversed.

fab_concentration.fact: TSMC Q3 2026 earnings call (15 Oct 2026): N2 is ramping in Hsinchu and Kaohsiung (Taiwan only); N3 output is ~180,000 wpm (Taiwan only, early Q4 2026 per TechTimes Aug 2026). Arizona Fab 21 Phase 2 (N3) has equipment installation underway but HVM targeted Q3 2027; Japan JASM Fab 2 (3nm) HVM 2028. Zero <=3nm wafers produced outside Taiwan as of today. Source: TSMC Q3 FY2026 earnings call via finance.biggo.com/quote/TSM/earnings-call/US_TSM_2026-10-15; corroborated by evertiq.com 2026-10-19 and techtimes.com 2026-08-08.
fab_concentration.rationale: All operational <=3nm (N3 and N2) capacity remains 100% in Taiwan; overseas fabs (Arizona Phase 2, Japan Fab 2) are in equipment installation or planning stages with no volume production until 2027-2028 at earliest. This places the share outside Taiwan at 0%, firmly within the rubric's EXTREME threshold of <10% with no operational overseas leading-edge fab.

dissent.view: PolicyRisk/SupplyMap projects Arizona Fab 21 Phase 2 will represent ~25% of global N3 capacity 'when fully ramped' — but this is a forward projection, not a current operational figure

hormuz_redsea_status.fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 2 commercial transits through the Strait of Hormuz on October 11 2026, against a pre-crisis baseline of ~85/day (~2% of baseline); Brent at ~$108/bbl; war-risk insurance at +2900% vs pre-crisis; 12 reported vessel strikes near Hormuz in the past week per UKMTO (CNN, Oct 17 2026); IRGC claims sea-mine strike south of strait on Oct 19 (straits.live/briefs/2026-10-19, sourcing IMF PortWatch).
hormuz_redsea_status.rationale: At 2% of baseline, Hormuz is far below the 25% threshold for CLOSED (score 2); Bab el-Mandeb traffic, while also disrupted and under active Houthi attack, is materially higher and is not the binding constraint. The rubric mandates rating the worse chokepoint, which is unambiguously Hormuz at 2 transits/day.

dissent.view: US CentCom disputed the full-closure picture in early October, claiming 20 million barrels of crude still moving through; some tankers transit with AIS off and are not counted by PortWatch, so true flow may be marginally higher than 2 vessels/day

cable_incidents.fact: Asia Times (published ~19 Sep 2026) reported that on 16 August 2026, the Wall Street Journal reported the Iranian government was considering attacks on Gulf submarine cable networks; state-affiliated Iranian media issued veiled threats of cable damage in the Strait of Hormuz. SubmarineCableStatus.com (checked 18 Oct 2026) lists no current Red Sea, Baltic, or Hormuz cable fault. The September 2025 Red Sea cuts (SMW4, IMEWE, FALCON GCX, EIG) are >13 months old and not listed as unrepaired.
cable_incidents.rationale: No major cable in the Red Sea, Baltic, or Hormuz is confirmed severed and unrepaired today, so rubric level 2 does not apply. Iran's credible, government-linked threats to Hormuz cables (Aug-Sep 2026) satisfy rubric level 1 ('credible official threats'). The prior load-bearing fact (Sept 2025 Red Sea cuts) is now outside the 90-day window and presumed repaired.
cable_incidents.change_reason: new_event: Iran government consideration of Hormuz cable attacks reported by WSJ on 16 Aug 2026, and corroborated by Asia Times Sep 2026 — replacing the expired Sept 2025 Red Sea cut as the load-bearing fact, while value remains 1

treasury_clearing_rollout.fact: DTCC/FICC GSD Member Survey (July 27, 2026): 79% of Netting Members have required FICC account structures in place; ~$1.2T in daily Treasury cash activity already clearing vs. $300-400B remaining; DTCC head Richard Kim (Oct 1, 2026, Finadium): 'majority of the US market is ready' for Dec 31 deadline, but urgency flagged for laggards. Simultaneously, SEC April 20, 2026 update (Commissioner Uyeda) confirms two exemptive relief requests -- SIFMA inter-affiliate and IIB extraterritorial -- remain open for public comment with no final relief granted. June 2026 Pulse Survey (DTCC/SIFMA): 72% of firms need more regulatory clarity; 88% of delayed buy-side programs cite legal/documentation as dominant constraint; 74% of sell-side cite tech build delays. No deadline extension has been announced; SEC Chair Atkins reaffirmed Dec 31, 2026 deadline on March 10, 2026.
treasury_clearing_rollout.rationale: Operational readiness has materially improved (79% account setup, $1.2T+ already clearing, broad onboarding pipeline) but two pending unresolved SEC exemptive relief requests (inter-affiliate and extraterritorial scoping) and a 72% regulatory-clarity gap among respondents sustain a documentation/regulatory-clarity backlog squarely in the FRICTION band (score 1); no deadline extension or operational failure has occurred to warrant score 2, and unresolved relief requests preclude SMOOTH (score 0).

dissent.view: DTCC Oct 1 2026 characterization ('majority ready') could support a downgrade toward SMOOTH (0) given 79% account setup and $1.2T already clearing; however, two open exemptive relief requests with no final SEC action and 72% regulatory-clarity gap in the June Pulse Survey prevent this reading.

oat_bund.fact: As of 19 October 2026, the 10-year OAT/Bund spread stands at 142.3 basis points (10Y OAT 4.85%, 10Y Bund 3.43%), per ideal-investisseur.fr citing Banque de France & Deutsche Bundesbank official data; intraday sources (ZeroHedge, Admiral Markets) corroborate a range of 142-146 bps on the same date.
oat_bund.rationale: 142.3 bps = 1.423 percentage points; this is the official close reading sourced from Banque de France & Bundesbank data for 19 Oct 2026, the most current available, well within the last 7 days window required by the rubric.
oat_bund.change_reason: new_event: Weekend civil unrest across France (19 Oct 2026) and proximity of Moody's sovereign review (23 Oct) drove OATs sharply wider on Monday morning, pushing the spread from 137.4 bps on 16 Oct to 142.3 bps at close on 19 Oct.

dissent.view: ING's Francesco Pesole (via Yahoo Finance/Investing.com, 19 Oct 2026) put the spread at 135-140 bps intraday, a lower intraday estimate than the official close
ZeroHedge (19 Oct 2026) cited an intraday peak of 146 bps and a c.144 bps level, above the official Banque de France closing figure of 142.3 bps
